name: Shallum
overview: Shallum was a male Levite, specifically an Aaronic priest descended through Eleazar. He is identified as the son of Zadok and the father of Hilkiah, situating him within a significant priestly lineage. His role as a Levite underscores his service and dedication to the worship and duties prescribed by God to the tribe of Levi.
namesAndTitles: The name Shallum means 'peace, well-being, prosperity,' reflecting a hopeful or blessed condition. He is also known by the name Meshullam, which means 'restitution.' Both names are proper names not given directly by God, indicating personal or familial significance rather than divine naming.
familyAndRelationships: Shallum is recorded as the son of Zadok and the father of Hilkiah, establishing a clear generational link in the priestly line. These relationships are explicitly noted in Scripture, emphasizing his place within the Levitical family tree.
scriptureSignificance: Shallum's importance lies in his priestly heritage and role within the Levitical tribe, serving as a direct descendant of the high priestly line through Eleazar. His position as father to Hilkiah connects him to subsequent key priestly figures, highlighting the continuity of God's ordained priesthood. This lineage reflects God's faithfulness in preserving the ministry through chosen families, vital for the worship life of Israel.
